t71a_jl2a.headline: AI Generated
flagged: AI-Generated (73 words): Regular breathing is fine for this, nothing fancy. It isn't asking you to forgive whoever hurt you either, or to picture their sad childhood. Calling them up is a whole separate decision, one for a day when you're less flooded. What it can do is take off some weight, that idea that feeling this proves you're the broken one, when plenty of people are feeling it right along with you.

t71a_oib.headline: AI Generated
flagged: AI-Generated (72 words): Here's a simple one. In the morning, set one small intention, like "Today I'll notice one hook before I act on it." At night, go over the day without putting yourself on trial: where you caught the hook, and where it ran its whole routine anyway (you'll probably find both). Then think of the next small repair, or something that would protect your little one a bit more tomorrow.

t71a_oia.headline: AI Generated
flagged: AI-Generated (76 words): Mornings get one small intention, something like "Today I'll notice one hook before I act on it." Just the one. At night you look back over the day with the kind eyes of a friend reading over your shoulder. Where did you catch the hook? Where did it run the whole routine anyway, before you noticed? And what's the next small repair, or the next thing you could do to protect your little one?

t71a_cs1a.headline: AI Generated
flagged: AI-Generated (70 words): Every session needs a real ending, or the processing just keeps going, and that can turn into one more way to avoid living. So look around and say where you are, even if it's only "my living room, the cat's here." Feel your feet on the floor, or the chair holding you up. Your jaw and hands have probably been clenching this whole time, so let them go.

t71a_jw2b.headline: AI Generated
flagged: AI-Generated (69 words): If writing about your feelings ties you in knots, there's a lower-tech version too. Jot the date and what helped, or just leave yourself a voice note. Nobody has to work out what it all means while they're writing it. Patterns can show up later, if they show up at all, and a memory aid doesn't have to explain your life to do its job.

t71a_jw2a.headline: AI Generated
flagged: AI-Generated (64 words): And if writing it all out just makes everything murkier, skip the meaning-making while you write. A few dated facts will do, like what happened and what helped, or a voice note on your phone, whatever keeps track of things. Patterns can wait until later, if they turn out to matter. A memory aid gets to be as dull as a grocery list.

t71a_jwb.headline: AI Generated
flagged: AI-Generated (94 words): Sometimes you ask and get silence, and then you're just sitting there wondering if you're doing it wrong. Try writing instead, with your wrong hand, the clumsy one whose letters already look like a little kid's. Whatever scared or hurt feelings are really there go on the page, nothing invented. Your good hand writes back as the grown-up, doing whichever of its three jobs is needed. And if the protective part shows up first, it gets the clumsy hand and its say before anyone asks your little one for theirs.

t71a_secsp5p23.headline: AI Generated

AI-Generated (119 words): Does saying it make the memory fiction? Well, no, it's still what happened, as far as you remember it, even if some details turn out fuzzy. And nobody's off the hook (you included, if you were the one who did it): whatever repair is owed is still owed. If the line helps, keep it to the one line.
Keep an ear on the narrator, though. If they start to sneer, stop. Stop too if you feel more ashamed, or kind of unreal, because telling it colder won't help with that. When it does help, you can ask what the younger you in that story needs from you now, and maybe give them a bit of it.

t71a_jwa.headline: AI Generated
flagged: AI-Generated (94 words): If talking or picturing gets you nothing but silence, try paper. Write with your wrong hand, the clumsy one whose letters already look like a first grader's, and put down whatever scared or hurt feelings are really there (no making things up for your little one). Then answer with your good hand, as the grown-up, doing whichever of its three jobs is needed. Does the protective part grab the pen first? Then it gets the wrong hand first, until it's had its say, and your little one can wait their turn.
